identity.flavour: glass kilns and the fallen star
identity.trade: Glass and ember-crystal: a star fell here in the old days, and Emberfall's glassblowers have worked its red glass since.
identity.tagline: Glass Kilns and the Fallen Star

greeting: Tithe day is never early and always too soon.
Careful. Some of this is fragile and some is merely valuable.
rumour: Strangers stop here more than they used to. Not all of them buy anything.
Lenses grown near the crater see further than lenses grown anywhere else.
Wind from the south brings spice, the west brings cold. Wind from the Scar brings nothing, and that is worse.

opinions.dalla_mossop: Dalla works hard and talks harder.
opinions.larkin_lensley: Larkin and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

time.morning: Morning. The experiment is running, so keep your voice down.

dialogue.aside: What did you see on the road? Tell me every bit. I will keep the details.

greeting: Sit anywhere that is not wet. The wet ones are the regulars.
Emberfall is glass kilns and the fallen star. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Scholars pay in ideas, mostly. I accept coin. I even accept the odd formula.
Travellers say the stones are dimmer on the east road. I water the ale, not the news.
The crystal in the kiln hums at night. We measured it. It matches no known note.
Every few years Emberfall has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.gwen_radcliffe: Gwen keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Evening. The light is best now for reading and worst for remembering.

dialogue.aside: Argh! Oh, it is you. Sorry. The kettle and I had words. Sit.

greeting: Mind the anvil. It has opinions.
Welcome to Emberfall. Mind the Emberfall Glass Kiln. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Tongs, crucible hooks, lens frames. Fine work, fussy customers.
Good steel is dear. Bad steel is dearer, the day it breaks.
The glass came out the wrong colour. Red where it should be clear. It was beautiful.

opinions.bartle_hallam: Bartle keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.night: Lamps at night. We call it work. Everyone else calls it madness.

dialogue.aside: Hmph. You again. Fine. Sit. I did not say I was glad.

greeting: Take your time. Touch nothing you cannot afford.
First time in Emberfall? The Emberfall Glass Kiln is the place to start.
rumour: Ink and quills go first. Then sand, then wax. Scholars lose pens like breath.
Candles are short this month. The wax comes late, and so does the honest news.
A lens ground last week shows a second moon. We wrote it down and told no one.
The Emberfall Glass Kiln was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.hewitt_elder: I would trust Hewitt with a purse. A small one.

time.rain: Rain. The roof leaks onto the third shelf. Move the books, move the books.

dialogue.aside: Smell the air, friend. Rain by supper. Bring a cloak, or come in.

greeting: You are somebody's grandchild. I can tell by the walk.
Emberfall is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: When I was young the stones sang at dusk. Now they hum, like someone ill.
Scholars from the Academy asked about the old star. We told them it is a rock.
A fallen-star fragment went missing from the kiln. The glass was bluer the next day.

opinions.hugh_lensley: Hugh works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Morning. The experiment is running, so keep your voice down.

dialogue.aside: Knock on wood, friend. Now touch iron. There. Safe, for a while.

greeting: Red glass, hot and honest. Mind the heat.
The Emberfall Glass Kiln is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Ember-crystal turns up in the sand after rain. Small, warm to the touch. We leave it.
The apprentice who copies the old notes began humming a tune the notes do not contain.

opinions.alys_mattock: Alys knows the trade. I will say that for Alys.

time.evening: Evening. The light is best now for reading and worst for remembering.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Oil, wick, glass. The glass is the hard part.
I have a theory. It is not finished. Neither is my tea.
rumour: Orders doubled since autumn. People want light they can carry.
A visitor from the Academy measured the kiln glow with a brass instrument and went pale.
The lantern makers of Silverford pay in silver for Emberfall red glass.

opinions.bettany_marlowe: Bettany knows the trade. I will say that for Bettany.
opinions.dorrit_greaves: Dorrit lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.night: Lamps at night. We call it work. Everyone else calls it madness.

dialogue.aside: You know me. You know my work. I will not insult either by modesty.

greeting: Out at dusk, back at dawn. Sleep is for the rich.
Folk come to Emberfall for glass kilns and the fallen star. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: The catch is bigger at night. The nights are longer. Odd arithmetic.
A lamp lit itself in the cold room. We checked the wick. No fault.
Whatever you hear about Emberfall, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.alys_mattock: Alys knows the trade. I will say that for Alys.
opinions.hewitt_elder: Hewitt lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.rain: Rain. The roof leaks onto the third shelf. Move the books, move the books.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. Let me look at you a moment. Fine. You pass. Come in.

greeting: Do not breathe on it. It is thinking.
Strangers in Emberfall get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: A pane came out with a figure in it, tall and hooded. I broke it. It came out again the next day.
The glassworkers argue over whether the crystal is growing or the room is shrinking.

opinions.bettany_marlowe: Bettany knows the trade. I will say that for Bettany.
opinions.dorrit_greaves: Dorrit works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Morning. The experiment is running, so keep your voice down.

dialogue.aside: Mind the order of things, friend. There. Now we can talk.

greeting: If it is not written down, it did not happen.
Do not touch the apparatus. If you must, use the left hand.
rumour: The ledgers say one thing. The cellars say another. I am only the scribe.
The books say the fallen star is dead. The kiln says otherwise.
Emberfall lives by glass kilns and the fallen star. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.alys_mattock: Alys keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.dorrit_greaves: Dorrit works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Evening. The light is best now for reading and worst for remembering.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. Let me look at you a moment. Fine. You pass. Come in.

greeting: A lamp is only a promise to come home. Buy two.
You will hear Emberfall before you see it. Ask at the Emberfall Glass Kiln.
rumour: One lamp burns blue and will not go out. Nobody has bought it. Nobody will.
Folk say Emberfall was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.alys_mattock: Alys works hard and talks harder.
opinions.hewitt_elder: Hewitt knows the trade. I will say that for Hewitt.

time.night: Lamps at night. We call it work. Everyone else calls it madness.

dialogue.aside: You look tired, friend. I will not lie. Rest.

greeting: Are you a soldier? You look like a soldier.
rumour: Our dog knows something and will not say what.
Lenses grown near the crater see further than lenses grown anywhere else.

opinions.hugh_lensley: Hugh and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

clues.note: A circle of scorch on the kiln-yard stone, too neat for an accident.
A crate lid nailed back crooked. The nails are bright.
The kiln log skips an hour. It is the hour the glass vanished in.
A paper nest, half burned, the ash still warm.
A dead rat, hollow, with a neat round hole in it.
A glove stained at the fingertips and swollen with something yellow.

stashes.say: You lift three cooled blanks from the annealing rack.
